items.title: Lorraine Feather interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 22, 2023
items.q: my friend was going there, Jeri Southern’s daughter Kathryn King.

ctx.x: You moved to Los Angeles and then you returned to New York. Do you recall if your parents were supportive of your intentions for a career in music?

Well at the time I was trying to have a career in theater because I had — I started taking dance lessons when I was 12. My mom, I think she was under the impression that it was cotillion or something, that I was going to make friends and meet people. And it wasn’t like that. It was a jazz dance class led by this guy Carlton Johnson who is fantastic. He’s not with us anymore but they had a conga player for the exercises and then they would play Motown music and I got totally smitten and started taking class…

award for some little competition. And then at 18 — well actually 17, I got a little scholarship to study at Circle in the Square, a theater in New York. And then I stayed on when I was 18 and got a waitress job, my friend joined me and got a waitress job and I proceeded to waitress a lot and occasionally I would get into a show. But your original question was do you recall how your parents felt about it?
